thesisQuality.note: Strong permitted high-grade project with construction underway, but value capture remains pre-production.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Construction progress and profitable uranium inventory monetization support funding; operating mine cash flow is not yet established.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Current equity value near US$2.57B is not obviously cheap against Phoenix C$1.57B base-case post-tax NPV8 without broader normalization; balanced/mixed band is warranted.

catalystScore.note: Concrete construction milestones and targeted mid-2028 first production provide material identifiable catalysts, with schedule risk remaining.

governancePower.note: Board advanced Phoenix through FID/permitting and management monetized uranium inventory above acquisition cost without equity dilution; long-duration capital-allocation proof remains incomplete.

alignment2036.note: Phoenix can add sizeable uranium supply into a durable nuclear-fuel need before decade end; this is strong long-duration infrastructure alignment.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Evidence is concentrated around Phoenix/Wheeler River and uranium; some inventory and other asset exposure exists but independent demand engines are not strongly demonstrated here.

bottleneckControl.note: Fully licensed construction-stage Canadian uranium capacity is scarce and Phoenix is positioned as meaningful new supply, but Denison does not control the uranium market itself.

scenarioRobustness.note: Funding buffer and physical uranium sales improve resilience, but thesis remains concentrated on Phoenix execution and uranium economics.

substitutionResilience.note: Licensed high-grade uranium supply has meaningful qualification/resource barriers, while alternative uranium suppliers remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.note: Engineering/procurement and construction readiness reduce some delivery risk, but greenfield remote construction retains meaningful supplier/logistics dependencies.

pricingPower.note: Recent uranium sales realized strong gains and contracted future deliveries at attractive prices, but mine-level durable pricing power is not yet demonstrated.

risk.note: Moderate-high execution risk from pre-production construction, ISR scale-up, capex/schedule and uranium-price sensitivity; permitting risk has materially declined.

confidence.note: Recent primary project/financial evidence plus independent current market valuation supports all components; confidence is reduced for future operating performance, customer diversification and mine-level pricing power.

thesis: Denison offers a permitted, construction-stage path to meaningful new Canadian uranium supply with unusually strong project economics and non-equity funding support, offset by pre-production execution concentration and a valuation that already recognizes substantial project value.
keyRisk: Phoenix construction/ISR scale-up or uranium-price weakness could impair economics before recurring mine cash flow is established.
nextCatalyst: Execution of 2026-2027 Phoenix construction milestones toward targeted mid-2028 first production.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore is the methodology-weighted component base; risk and confidence are separately source-addressed for downstream methodology treatment.
